title: Nonlinear Equations and Systems, Part 2: Medium and Hard Problems

beats.say: In part one, we solved a quadratic by factoring, and we saw that the discriminant counts the real solutions.
In this video, we solve a radical equation and check for a false solution, and then find a constant using the discriminant.
Medium example. Solve the radical equation, the square root of x plus seven equals x minus five. Squaring both sides is the usual first step, but it can create a false solution.
Our plan is to square both sides to remove the radical, solve the quadratic, and then check every answer in the original equation.
Square both sides. The left side becomes x plus seven. The right side becomes x minus five, squared, which we must expand carefully.
Expand the square. x minus five, squared, is x squared minus ten x plus twenty-five.
Move everything to one side. Subtract x and seven from both sides, so the left side becomes zero.
beats.op: move all terms to one side

beats.say: Factor. We need two numbers that multiply to eighteen and add to negative eleven. Those are negative two and negative nine.
The candidates are x equals two and x equals nine. Check x equals two. The square root of nine is three, but two minus five is negative three. They do not match, so two is extraneous.
Now check x equals nine. The square root of sixteen is four, and nine minus five is four. They match. So the only solution is x equals nine.
Hard example. For what positive value of k does x squared minus k x plus sixteen equal zero have exactly one real solution?
Exactly one real solution means the discriminant is zero. Here a is one, b is negative k, and c is sixteen. So we set b squared minus four a c equal to zero.

scenes.title: Hard: set the discriminant to zero

beats.say: Substitute a equals one, b equals negative k, and c equals sixteen. Notice that b is squared, so the negative sign disappears.
Negative k, squared, is k squared. Four times one times sixteen is sixty-four.
Add sixty-four to both sides, so that k squared stands alone on the left side of the equation.
Take the square root of both sides. Remember that there are two roots, positive eight and negative eight.
The question asks for the positive value of k. So k equals eight.
Check by substituting k equals eight. The equation becomes x squared minus eight x plus sixteen, which is x minus four, squared. That is zero only at x equals four, so there is exactly one solution.
beats.verdict: Zero only at x = 4. One solution.

beats.say: To recap. After squaring both sides of a radical equation, always check every candidate in the original equation.
Exactly one solution means a discriminant of zero. Remember that b is squared, so its sign does not matter.
Read the question for which value it wants, such as the positive one. In the next video, we look at common traps and the fast way with Desmos.
